newsitem.title: UK: Licht sees stable world sugar prices into 1997/98.
newsitem.headline: Licht sees stable world sugar prices into 1997/98.

text.p: World sugar markets could see another year of stable prices into 1997/98 as the prospect of a limited stocks drawdown supports sentiment, German statistician F.O. Licht said on Thursday.
In its third estimate of the world 1996/97 sugar balance, Licht said it had cut its production figure by just 0.6 percent from the initial forecast and increased consumption by less than 1.0 percent.
"In such stable conditions it is hardly surprising that there has been a high degree of price stability." Licht said.
"Right now no earth shaking changes are on the horizon and we may see another year of fairly stable prices with a slightly positive note."
Much of the price stability in recent weeks could be attributed to lower crop expectations for 1997/98 and another healthy rise in sugar offtake.
A consumption figure of 123 million tonnes for 1997/98 should not be too far off the mark, the report said.
Sugar production was more difficult to assess due to weather factors but current indications suggested that it will not change greatly.
"If this assessment should prove to be correct, then taking into account unrecorded disappearance, a limited draw down of stocks seems to be on the cards," it said.
"But it is still very early days and the market may not prove to be as dull as appears now." --Jeremy Smith, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8064
